Object: TO FIND THE APPROXIMATE pH OF SOME SOLUTIONs USING UNIVERSAL INDICATOR AND pH PAPER

A universal indicator or a pH paper contains a mixture of several acidbase indicators and hence can show several colour changes over a wide range of pH values. Hence it can be conveniently used to determine the approximate pH of any solution. pH of a solution can be defined as the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion or hydronium ion concentration. pH = - log[H+] or, = log [H30+1
A. Using universal indicator 1, Take 10ml of different juices or samples in different test tubes with the help of a measuring cylinder.
2. Add 3 drops of universal indicator into each and shake well.
3. Note the colour developed in each sample and compare with the
colour chart given on the universal indicator bottle.
4. Note down the approximate pH of each sample.

Object: TO FIND THE PERCENTAGE LOSS IN VVEIGHT OFA
HYDRATED SALT ON HEATING AND TO FIND NUMBER OF
MOLES OF WATER OF CRYSTALLIZATION PRESENT IN IT
Many of the substances are found to lose their water of crystallization or to be decomposed evolving the gases like C02, N02 etc. while heating.
Due to this, weight of the substances is lost. Then the percentage loss in weight is calculated as:
Weight of water or gas lost % loss in weight = Weight of hydrated salt The number of moles of water of crystallization in a mole of the hydrated salt can be determined as:

Weight of water in gram that combines with 1 mole of anhydrous salt Number of moles of water = Molecular weight of water The water of crystallization is responsible for crystalline property Of all hydrated salts.
Hydrated salt Crucible Sand bath Figure 6.1: Heating of hydrated salt
Take a crucible with lid and weigh out it accurately.
Take about 1 gram of the given hydrated salt in this crucible. Weigh the crucible with lid. Note the weight.
Heat the crucible strongly with lid slightly opened for about 15 minutes.
Cool the crucible by placing it over asbestos sheet and then in a desiccator. Weigh the crucible with lid. Note the weight.
Heat the crucible again as in No. (3). Weigh the crucible again after cooling. Note the weight.
Repeat the process of heating, cooling and weighing till the weight is found to be constant. Note the constant weight.

Weight of crucible + lid = WI gm Weight of crucible + lid + hydrated salt = W2 gm Weight of crucible + lid + residue (constant weight) = W3 gm Now, Weight of hydrated salt = (W2 — WI) gm Weight of anhydrous salt (residue) = (W3 — WI) gm Weight of water lost = (W2 — WI) — (W3 — WI) gm = (W2 — W3) gm To find the % loss in weight:
